The Cloudrunner
(Crateromys schadenbergi) 
 
 (also known as the giant bushy-tailed cloud rat) is endemic to the mossy oak and pine forests of the Cordillera Central mountain range. The Luzon Cloudrunner is a nocturnal, arboreal (tree-dwelling) mammal spending its life high in the tree canopy feeding on tender leaves, buds, and fruit. Because they rely entirely on thick forest cover, cloudrunners are vulnerable to slash-and-burn agriculture (kaingin) and logging. By mapping and actively establishing strict firebreaks, the Mabaka tribe ensures that the dense canopy remains intact, preventing the slow-reproducing animals from losing their arboreal pathways.
